title: Plea bargaining in India - why lawyers rarely use this option
p1:
Many accused persons don't know they have another path besides a long criminal trial.

India has a legal option that can sometimes end a case faster — but it is rarely discussed.
p2:
The common belief is that every criminal case must go through a full trial. But plea bargaining allows an accused person to accept responsibility for certain offences in exchange for a possible reduction in punishment or a quicker resolution.

The surprising part? Even though this option exists in Indian law, many lawyers and accused persons hesitate to use it.
p3:
One reason is perception. Many fear that accepting a plea may look like admitting guilt, while others prefer to fight for complete acquittal. There are also restrictions on which offences qualify, making the option unavailable in many serious cases.

The practical takeaway: plea bargaining is not about escaping justice. It is a legal mechanism designed to reduce delays and help courts focus on cases that truly need a full trial.
